---
title: "4 · CNNs, Class Activation Maps, Adversarial Examples and the 2D Ising Model"
code-tools: false
toc: false
---

Convolutional networks use the spatial structure of images. We build them on CIFAR-10 from convolution kernels such as Sobel filters, with stride, padding, channels and pooling, and regularise them with L1 and L2 penalties, dropout and batch normalisation. Class activation maps and Grad-CAM show which image regions drive a prediction, and adversarial examples show how small perturbations change it. A survey of optimisers leads from stochastic gradient descent to Adam. The second half of the lecture turns to the 2D Ising model. We introduce its partition function, the exact solution of the 1D chain and Onsager's solution in 2D, critical behaviour, mean field, universality and Metropolis sampling. A CNN trained only far from the transition then classifies configurations at all temperatures, and its confidence drops near the critical temperature for lattice sizes from 10 to 50. The lecture ends with the Chinese Room thought experiment.
